entries.clinical_indication: Definitive chemoradiation for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (larynx, oropharynx, hypopharynx) or postoperative adjuvant CRT for high-risk resected disease with positive margins or extranodal extension (ENE)

regimen_components.frequency: Every 21 days on days 1, 22, and 43

prehydration_and_hydration.prehydration: 1000 mL Normal Saline (0.9% NaCl) + 20 mEq KCl + 1 g MgSO4 IV over 2 to 3 hours prior to cisplatin infusion
prehydration_and_hydration.mannitol_or_diuretic: Mannitol 12.5-25 g IV given over 15 minutes before or during cisplatin to ensure brisk diuresis
prehydration_and_hydration.posthydration: 1000-2000 mL Normal Saline + 20 mEq KCl IV over 4 to 6 hours post-infusion
prehydration_and_hydration.urine_output_target: Maintain urine output >= 100 mL/hr during infusion and for 4 hours post-infusion

antiemetic_protocol.emetogenic_risk: High emetogenic risk (>90% frequency of emesis without antiemetics)
antiemetic_protocol.regimen: Four-drug combination: (1) NK1 receptor antagonist: Aprepitant 125 mg PO d1, then 80 mg PO d2-3 (or Fosaprepitant 150 mg IV d1); (2) 5-HT3 receptor antagonist: Ondansetron 8-16 mg IV/PO or Palonosetron 0.25 mg IV d1; (3) Dexamethasone 12 mg PO/IV d1, then 8 mg PO daily d2-4; (4) Olanzapine 5-10 mg PO daily on days 1-4

eligibility_thresholds.audiogram: No severe pre-existing sensorineural high-frequency hearing loss or disabling tinnitus
eligibility_thresholds.neuropathy: No pre-existing peripheral sensory neuropathy >= Grade 2

dose_modifications.crcl_50_to_59: Reduce cisplatin dose by 25-50% or switch to weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2) or carboplatin AUC 4-5
dose_modifications.crcl_less_than_50: Cisplatin absolutely contraindicated. Switch to Carboplatin (AUC 4-5) or Cetuximab (400 load / 250 weekly) or RT alone
dose_modifications.neutrophil_nadir: Delay cycle if ANC < 1.5 x 10^9/L or Plt < 100 x 10^9/L until recovery; reduce dose by 25% for febrile neutropenia
dose_modifications.ototoxicity: Discontinue cisplatin and switch to alternative if new >= Grade 2 hearing loss develops

entries.protocol_name: Weekly Cisplatin Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy for Cervical Cancer
entries.clinical_indication: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced cervical carcinoma (FIGO Stage IB2 to IVA) or postoperative high-risk resected disease

regimen_components.frequency: Weekly (days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29; up to 6 cycles max)

prehydration_and_hydration.prehydration: 1000 mL Normal Saline IV over 1-2 hours prior to weekly cisplatin
prehydration_and_hydration.posthydration: Encourage oral fluids (2 liters/day) or administer 500-1000 mL Normal Saline post-infusion
prehydration_and_hydration.urine_output_target: Maintain brisk urine output during infusion

antiemetic_protocol.regimen: Two-drug combination: (1) 5-HT3 receptor antagonist: Ondansetron 8 mg IV/PO 30 minutes prior to infusion; (2) Dexamethasone 8-12 mg IV/PO 30 minutes prior to infusion

dose_modifications.weekly_hold_criteria: Hold dose if ANC < 1.0 x 10^9/L, Platelets < 50 x 10^9/L, or serum creatinine > 1.5x baseline until recovery
dose_modifications.crcl_less_than_50: Switch to Carboplatin AUC 2 weekly if renal impairment develops or persists

entries.protocol_name: CROSS Neoadjuvant Carboplatin and Paclitaxel Chemoradiation
entries.clinical_indication: Neoadjuvant chemoradiation for resectable esophageal or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma

regimen_components.frequency: Weekly on days 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29

regimen_components.route: IV infusion over 30 minutes (Calvert formula: Dose = AUC x [CrCl + 25])
regimen_components.frequency: Weekly on days 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 following paclitaxel

prehydration_and_hydration.premedication: Dexamethasone 20 mg PO 12h and 6h prior to paclitaxel (or 10-20 mg IV 30 min prior), Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV 30 min prior, and Famotidine 20 mg IV 30 min prior to prevent hypersensitivity reactions

antiemetic_protocol.regimen: Ondansetron 8 mg IV + Dexamethasone 10-20 mg IV pre-chemotherapy

eligibility_thresholds.creatinine_clearance: CrCl >= 30 mL/min (Calvert formula caps CrCl at 125 mL/min)

dose_modifications.hematologic: Hold weekly dose if ANC < 1.0 x 10^9/L or Platelets < 75 x 10^9/L until recovery; reduce paclitaxel to 40 mg/m2 and carboplatin to AUC 1.6 for febrile neutropenia
dose_modifications.neuropathy: Reduce paclitaxel by 20% for Grade 2 sensory neuropathy; hold for Grade >= 3 neuropathy

entries.clinical_indication: Consolidation immunotherapy in patients with unresectable Stage III NSCLC whose disease has not progressed after definitive concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy

regimen_components.frequency: Every 2 weeks (or fixed dose 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks)
regimen_components.duration: Up to 12 months (or until confirmed disease progression or unmanageable toxicity)
regimen_components.initiation_window: Commence within 1 to 42 days following completion of definitive chemoradiotherapy

prehydration_and_hydration.monitoring: Baseline and routine monitoring prior to each infusion: Complete metabolic panel (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin, creatinine), Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4), and clinical assessment for pneumonitis

antiemetic_protocol.emetogenic_risk: Minimal emetogenic risk (<10%); routine antiemetics not indicated

eligibility_thresholds.post_crt_status: No evidence of disease progression on post-CRT restaging chest CT
eligibility_thresholds.radiation_pneumonitis: Resolution of any acute radiation-related pneumonitis to <= Grade 1
eligibility_thresholds.autoimmune: No active severe autoimmune disease requiring systemic immunosuppression

dose_modifications.immune_pneumonitis_grade_2: Withhold durvalumab; initiate systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 1-2 mg/kg/day); resume durvalumab only after steroid taper and resolution to <= Grade 1
dose_modifications.immune_pneumonitis_grade_3_4: Permanently discontinue durvalumab; administer high-dose IV methylprednisolone (1-2 mg/kg/day); obtain urgent pulmonary and infectious disease consultation
dose_modifications.immune_hepatitis_grade_2: Withhold durvalumab for AST/ALT > 3x ULN or total bilirubin > 1.5x ULN; initiate prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day
dose_modifications.immune_hepatitis_grade_3_4: Permanently discontinue durvalumab for AST/ALT > 5x ULN or total bilirubin > 3x ULN; administer IV methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day

entries.protocol_name: Stupp Temozolomide Radiochemotherapy Protocol for Glioblastoma
entries.clinical_indication: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (WHO Grade 4 astrocytoma) or IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytic glioma

regimen_components.frequency: 7 days/week for 42 to 49 days throughout radiation therapy (60 Gy / 30 fx)
regimen_components.administration_instructions: Take orally on empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after food), 1 hour before radiation treatment on treatment days
regimen_components.mandatory_pjp_prophylaxis: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) 1 DS tablet PO 3 times weekly throughout concomitant phase

regimen_components.route: Oral daily on days 1 to 5 of 28-day cycle for Cycle 1; escalate to 200 mg/m2/day for Cycles 2-6 if no hematologic toxicity
regimen_components.frequency: Days 1-5 every 28 days for 6 cycles
regimen_components.initiation: Commences 4 weeks after completion of radiotherapy

antiemetic_protocol.emetogenic_risk: Moderate emetogenic risk during daily dosing
antiemetic_protocol.regimen: Ondansetron 4-8 mg PO taken 30-60 minutes prior to each temozolomide dose

eligibility_thresholds.absolute_neutrophil_count: ANC >= 1.5 x 10^9/L prior to starting and each cycle

dose_modifications.concomitant_phase_hold: Hold temozolomide if ANC < 1.5 x 10^9/L or Platelets < 100 x 10^9/L; discontinue if not recovered within 2 weeks
dose_modifications.adjuvant_cycle_escalation: Escalate to 200 mg/m2/day for Cycle 2 only if Cycle 1 nadir ANC >= 1.5 and Platelets >= 100
dose_modifications.adjuvant_dose_reduction: Reduce dose from 200 to 150 mg/m2 (or 150 to 100 mg/m2) if nadir ANC < 1.0 or Platelets < 50 x 10^9/L

entries.protocol_name: Nigro / ACT II 5-Fluorouracil and Mitomycin C Protocol
entries.clinical_indication: Definitive chemoradiotherapy for squamous cell / epidermoid carcinoma of the anal canal

regimen_components.route: Continuous IV infusion over 24 hours on days 1-4 (96-hour continuous infusion) and days 29-32
IV bolus on day 1 (capped at max 20 mg single dose)

antiemetic_protocol.regimen: Ondansetron 8 mg IV + Dexamethasone 10 mg IV on days of chemotherapy initiation

eligibility_thresholds.dpyd_testing: Recommend screening for DPYD deficiency prior to 5-FU initiation to prevent fatal fluoropyrimidine toxicity

dose_modifications.delayed_myelosuppression: Mitomycin causes delayed and cumulative myelosuppression with nadir at 4 to 6 weeks; monitor weekly CBC closely
dose_modifications.cycle_2_hold: Hold Day 29 5-FU if severe radiation proctitis/dermatitis >= Grade 3, ANC < 1.0, or Platelets < 75 until recovery

entries.clinical_indication: Adjuvant immunotherapy for patients with completely resected esophageal or gastroesophageal junction cancer with residual pathologic disease (ypT+ or ypN+) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy

regimen_components.frequency: Every 2 weeks for 16 weeks (8 doses)
Every 4 weeks starting at week 17 for a total treatment duration of 1 year

eligibility_thresholds.pathologic_status: Pathologically confirmed residual disease (>= ypT1 or ypN+) in surgical specimen; R0 resection required
eligibility_thresholds.organ_function: Adequate hepatic, renal, and endocrine function

dose_modifications.immune_adverse_events: Withhold for Grade 2 immune-mediated pneumonitis, colitis, or nephritis; discontinue permanently for Grade >= 3 toxicity

entries.protocol_name: RAPIDO Total Neoadjuvant Therapy CAPOX Consolidation Protocol
entries.clinical_indication: Consolidation chemotherapy following short-course radiotherapy (5x5 Gy) in high-risk locally advanced rectal cancer prior to TME surgery

regimen_components.route: IV infusion over 2 hours on day 1
regimen_components.frequency: Every 21 days for 6 cycles

regimen_components.route: Oral twice daily on days 1 to 14
regimen_components.frequency: Every 21 days for 6 cycles

antiemetic_protocol.regimen: Ondansetron 8 mg IV/PO + Dexamethasone 12 mg IV/PO on day 1

eligibility_thresholds.creatinine_clearance: CrCl >= 50 mL/min (reduce capecitabine by 25% for CrCl 30-49 mL/min)

dose_modifications.neurotoxicity: Hold or reduce oxaliplatin by 20% for persistent Grade >= 2 cold-induced or painful sensory neuropathy
dose_modifications.diarrhea: Hold capecitabine for Grade >= 2 diarrhea; restart with 25% dose reduction after complete resolution to Grade 0-1

entries.clinical_indication: Unfavorable intermediate-risk localized adenocarcinoma of the prostate in combination with definitive external beam radiotherapy

regimen_components.route: IM 3-month depot (or Goserelin 10.8 mg SC 3-month depot)
regimen_components.frequency: Given at Month 0 and Month 3 (total 4 to 6 months duration)
regimen_components.initiation: Initiated 2 months prior to start of radiotherapy (neoadjuvant, concurrent, and short adjuvant)

regimen_components.frequency: Daily starting 1-2 weeks prior to first LHRH injection and continuing for 2-4 weeks to block testosterone surge flare

eligibility_thresholds.baseline_workup: Baseline serum PSA, total testosterone, fasting lipid panel, glucose/HbA1c, liver function tests, and baseline DEXA scan

dose_modifications.alternative: GnRH antagonist (Degarelix 240 mg initial SC then 80 mg monthly or Relugolix 120 mg PO daily) avoids testosterone surge without requiring bicalutamide flare protection

entries.clinical_indication: High-risk or very high-risk localized or locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the prostate in combination with definitive radiotherapy

regimen_components.frequency: Every 3 to 6 months for a total duration of 24 to 36 months (2 to 3 years)
regimen_components.initiation: Initiated 2 to 3 months prior to radiotherapy and continued throughout RT and for 2-3 years adjuvantly

regimen_components.frequency: Daily for 2 to 4 weeks starting prior to initial LHRH agonist dose to prevent testosterone surge flare

supportive_care.bone_health: Baseline DEXA bone density scan; Calcium 1000-1200 mg daily + Vitamin D3 1000-2000 IU daily; consider Zoledronic acid 4 mg IV annually or Denosumab 60 mg SC q6m if osteopenic/osteoporotic
supportive_care.cardiometabolic: Monitor lipid profile, fasting blood glucose/HbA1c, and encourage resistance and aerobic exercise to prevent sarcopenic obesity and metabolic syndrome

eligibility_thresholds.stage_criteria: High-risk features: cT3-T4, or Gleason score 8-10, or initial PSA > 20 ng/mL

dose_modifications.duration: Standard duration is 24 to 36 months based on EORTC 22961 and RTOG 9202; 18 months may be considered in selected elderly patients with favorable biology
